mike: Quick heads-up — we've been seeing intermittent 429 spikes from the Go streaming client hitting hosted endpoints. Mostly short bursts, ~200-500ms windows, but clients are doing full reconnects and replays. Thinking we should update the default retry/backoff policy and add clearer guidance for idempotency/resume tokens. Anyone seen this recently?
sasha: Saw it in staging this morning. Repro: start a long-stream, auth refresh happens -> a few frames get 429, client tears down and restarts. We should try to resume instead of full restart.
raj: Agree. A couple notes: 1) honor Retry-After when present (HTTP/1.1 header) 2) use capped exponential with jitter for other 429/5xx 3) avoid retrying non-idempotent actions without explicit Idempotency-Key.
alice: +1. For streams we need two behaviors: resume-capable requests (can send a resume token to continue) vs restart-only requests. Resume requests: safe to back off+retry and attempt resume. Restart-only: treat like non-idempotent, fail fast or require user opt-in.
mike: Proposed default backoff config for Go SDK: initial=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max=8s, attempts=6, jitter=full-random (±50%). We should also add a small randomized base jitter to avoid thundering herd. Thoughts?
sasha: That seems reasonable. Suggest tweak: if Retry-After present, sleep exactly that duration (plus a small jitter). Also for 5xx prefer a slightly faster cap (max=4s) because those are often transient infra glitches and blocking long streams wastes resources.
raj: Implementation detail: prefer deterministic capped jitter function so we can test it. Example pseudocode I used:
```go
func Backoff(attempt int) time.Duration {
  base := 200 * time.Millisecond << uint(attempt) // exponential
  if base > 8*time.Second { base = 8*time.Second }
  jitter := time.Duration(rand.Int63n(int64(base/2))) - base/4 // ±25%
  return base + jitter
}
```
This keeps tests stable if we seed RNG.
alice: For idempotency header, recommend standard header name: "Idempotency-Key" (UUIDv4). For streams add a "Resume-Token" in the stream metadata. If server accepts resume token, client attempts resume and only replays missing deltas. Document both in SDK README with example.
mike: Good. Also need to update the docs page with a decision table: 429 -> if Retry-After present obey it; else backoff+retry (resume if supported). 5xx -> backoff+retry but smaller cap. 401 during stream -> try transparent token refresh once, then resume if possible, else surface error.
sasha: I'll attach repro logs in the PR. Notable log pattern:
```
HTTP 429 quota burst - client reconnecting
stream id=abc123 resume_token=rt-001
client: got 429 while sending frame seq=42
client: dropped connection, attempting backoff retry
```
Include that in the error-sensitivity tests.
raj: For non-resumable endpoints, add an opt-in flag like `RetryOnNonIdempotent bool` default=false. If user sets true, we try one retry after guarded backoff and annotate telemetry.
mike: Action items: Sasha -> open SDK PR with backoff implementation + tests; Raj -> add design note and test vectors for jitter; Alice -> doc snippet for Idempotency-Key and Resume-Token examples. I'll follow up to make the default config change.
sasha: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/4567 :sparkles: (WIP, tests failing but working on it).
devex-bot: CI started for PR #4567 — build queued.
mike: Awesome, thanks. Let's land the tests and update the changelog. After PR merges we'll flip a feature flag in hosted infra to accept Resume-Token header. :thumbsup:
raj: One last thing — add a small perf test that simulates 1% auth refresh/429s at scale to ensure backoff prevents connection storms.
alice: I'll add a short README snippet with sample Go usage:
```go
client := newClient(WithRetryPolicy(DefaultStreamRetry))
client.Stream(ctx, req, WithResumeToken("rt-001"))
```
Keep the examples minimal.
mike: Cool. If anyone wants to pair on the PR ping me, otherwise I'll review tomorrow.
